subject.title: RFC 0014: Pluggable scheduler seam in gateway

question: Should this RFC repository accept `kind: scheduler` plus `owns: scheduled-jobs` as the plugin-SDK direction for external scheduled-job ownership?
rationale: The remaining decision is whether this new plugin API and gateway ownership model belongs in OpenClaw; that product/API boundary cannot be settled by cleanup automation.

options.title: Accept the RFC direction
options.body: Merge the RFC as the approved design after updating `status` and `issue`, and require the documented implementation gates before runtime code lands.

options.title: Request a narrower contract
options.body: Keep the PR open and ask the author to reduce or reshape the scheduler ownership token, runtime functions, or run-state event surface before acceptance.

options.title: Reject core scheduler ownership
options.body: Close or redirect the idea if maintainers want external schedulers to remain behind public HTTP/plugin surfaces without a first-class gateway ownership seam.

recommendation.title: Accept the RFC direction
recommendation.body: Merge the RFC as the approved design after updating `status` and `issue`, and require the documented implementation gates before runtime code lands.

likelyOwner.reason: They have recent merged plugin/feed RFC history and broad RFC-tree activity, though final gateway/plugin API approval may also need OpenClaw core owners outside this repository.
